title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
authors: Seung Hwan Lee, Shaowen Chen, Andrew T. Pierce, Patrick R. Forrester, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Amir Yacoby
abstract: Two-dimensional material platforms now host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases, from unconventional superconductivity to fractional Chern insulators. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction - the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at $ν$ = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at $ν$ = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials.
summary: The authors report the first demonstration of magnon transmission across a quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction using MLG/BLG graphene. By generating magnons in the MLG source and detecting them nonlocally in the BLG target, they establish a powerful, all-electrical technique. This method successfully maps the magnetic order of the BLG quantum Hall states by observing characteristic signal features dependent on spin polarization.
main_problem: The challenge is to probe magnetic order in two-dimensional materials with dilute spin densities, where conventional magnetic probes are ineffective.
main_result: The study successfully demonstrates that magnon transmission across a graphene heterojunction (MLG/BLG) serves as a powerful, all-electrical method to map out the magnetic phase diagram of the target material.
method: Nonlocal voltage measurements ($	ext{SNL}$) are used to detect magnons generated in a source material (MLG) and transmitted into a target material (BLG) across a heterojunction.
model_or_system: The experiment utilizes a heterojunction between monolayer graphene (MLG) and bilayer graphene (BLG) operating in the Quantum Hall Ferromagnet (QHFM) regime. The mechanism relies on generating magnons via bias voltage exceeding the Zeeman energy in the source material.
key_observables: Nonlocal voltage signal ($	ext{SNL}$), two-terminal conductance ($g_{MLG}$), and the sharp onset of $	ext{SNL}$ at the Zeeman energy ($E_Z$).

paper_structure:
The paper establishes the physical necessity of the technique, details the measurement setup using MLG/BLG heterojunctions, demonstrates the magnon generation threshold via conductance measurements, and finally maps the magnetic order of the BLG state by observing the characteristic $	ext{SNL}$ features as a function of $

why_interesting: This work provides a novel, purely electrical spectroscopic tool to probe magnetic excitations (magnons) in correlated 2D electron systems, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phases in condensed matter.
